title: Alice and Bob Playing Flower Game
summary: Alice and Bob engage in a turn-based game on a field with two lanes of flowers.
statement: Alice and Bob engage in a turn-based game on a field with two lanes of flowers. Alice starts. Each turn, a player picks one flower from either lane. Alice wins if she can make the opponent pick the last flower, given x flowers in the first lane and y in the second. Calculate the number of (x, y) pairs where x is between 1 and n, y is between 1 and m, and Alice wins.
constraints: For each 1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= m, players alternately remove one flower and Alice moves first.
Count pairs for which Alice takes the last flower.
hints: Alice wins exactly when x+y is odd, meaning one lane count is odd and the other even.
Count odd and even choices independently in each range.
The two opposite-parity cases are disjoint and cover every winning pair.
editorial: The two opposite-parity cases are disjoint and cover every winning pair.

tests.explanation: Exactly the three pairs with opposite parities have an odd total and are winning.
Two total flowers let Bob take the last flower, so this pair is not winning for Alice.
